source.title: Thermodynamic Weight Decay: Exploring Grokking Acceleration via Attention Specific Heat

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It includes figure captions and tables, but not the underlying figure images.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on modular arithmetic and tests whether an attention-specific-heat signal can be used to alter its timing. It uses a new intervention rather than reproducing the original training recipe.
record.gate_note: Reports baseline and intervention grokking outcomes, per-seed grokking epochs, and attention-specific-heat precursor measurements. The initialization-noise, micro-ripple, and slingshot observations concern detector design; they do not establish the broader optimizer/numerical artifact claim in V7.
record.test_reason: On modular addition (a+b mod 97) with a 2-layer Transformer, the study reports baseline grokking epochs across 10 seeds, well after train accuracy saturates (V1). It measures a continuous attention-logit-variance signal (Cv) that peaks before grokking (V2-adjacent progress measure). It also tests whether raising weight decay enables or speeds grokking (V5-adjacent). The recipe differs from the originals: an added Cv-driven weight-decay controller.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Cv is a qualitative precursor (10/10 seeds) but not a timing predictor. They conclude that dynamic weight decay enables grokking within a fixed budget and modestly accelerates it. They limit these claims to one task and call the evidence statistically suggestive.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition and train/validation accuracy to study grokking, but adds Cv-based dynamic weight-decay schedules and a scale-invariant z-score controller. It does not vary training-set size.
record.method_sensitivity: The cold-start and continuous-sensor variants differ in performance; on seed 4096 they grok at epochs 2767 and 3078, respectively. The scale-invariant variant produces smaller peak dynamic weight decay (0.8–1.1) than the κ/τ variant (1.5–2.6). The paper reports that Cv peak timing does not strongly correlate with the eventual grokking epoch.
record.problems: Single task and small 2-layer Transformer; no training-set-size sweep; limited statistical power (10 seeds) and tests disagree; no weight-decay schedule control separating the Cv signal from the effect of applying more weight decay; no direct circuit identification or comparison with other progress measures.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the per-seed grokking-epoch table or main comparison. Detector-development failures (initialization trigger at epoch 16, micro-ripple trigger at epoch 240, and one slingshot-related gate failure) are summarized in gate_note rather than entered as claim-version outcomes.

untested.parts: There is no training-set-size sweep, so the claim that the delay grows as data shrinks is untested.
No generalizing circuit or Fourier algorithm is identified, and there is no evidence on the removal of memorizing components.
Not tested: there is no non-algorithmic data and no init-scale or weight-norm sweep.
Not tested: there is no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Efficiency of the generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, and ungrokking are all untested.
Not tested: learned algorithms are not compared across runs.
Not tested: there are no optimizer or floating-point controls.

missing.what: Aggregate for the continuous-sensor variant versus baseline: mean 4333 vs 4313, i.e. no improvement despite added weight decay.
The κ/τ study (5 seeds, 10,000 epochs) is described in the setup, but its grokking outcomes are not reported beyond peak weight decay of 1.5-2.6.
Applying weight decay before memorization (ungated trigger at epoch 16) performed worse than baseline. No number is given.

record.verdict_notes: The Cv-driven method is the study's own intervention. The V5 bearing rests only on 'more weight decay helps grokking', which the authors note is not separated from the Cv signal. V5's distinctive predictions are untested. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether smaller training sets require more optimization. The per-seed table reports threshold-crossing epochs, not full train/validation accuracy trajectories for every seed.
Measures attention specific heat as a precursor, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, measure Fourier-algorithm formation, or show memorizing components being removed.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule data; no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Tests dynamic weight-decay interventions and generalization outcomes, but does not test whether a more efficient circuit is favored, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
Does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
Does not test whether grokking is an adaptive-optimizer or floating-point artifact, or whether controls for those effects remove the delay.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer (dmodel = 128, 4 heads, dk = 32, RoPE, GELU), aggregate over 10 paired seeds
rows.operation_detail: Paired comparison of baseline AdamW with cold-start scale-invariant CvAdamW.
rows.measure: Mean grokking latency and paired improvement
rows.value: Cold-start mean 4056 epochs; mean reduction 257 epochs (6.0%); median reduction 166 epochs (4.3%); cold-start better on 8/10 seeds.
rows.uncertainty: Wilcoxon W = 8, p = 0.049; paired t-test t(9) = 2.15, p = 0.060; sign test p = 0.109; bootstrap 95% CI [53, 489] epochs; classical 95% CI [−13, 527] epochs; Cohen’s d = 0.68.
rows.note: Authors characterize the evidence as suggestive and mixed; statistical tests disagree at n = 10.
rows.check: This paired comparison is the method versus baseline, not a test of V1. The weight-decay effect is modest: mean -257 epochs (6%), with the tests disagreeing (t-test p=0.060, sign test p=0.109). There is no control separating more weight decay from Cv timing.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer (dmodel = 128, 4 heads, dk = 32, RoPE, GELU), aggregate over 10 seeds
rows.operation_detail: Locate the post-memorization peak of EMA-smoothed attention specific heat on baseline trajectories and compare it with grokking.
rows.measure: Whether Cv peak precedes grokking; lead time
rows.baseline: Grokking epoch is the reference event.
rows.value: Cv peaks before grokking in 10/10 seeds; mean lead time 2400 epochs, std 974, median 2396.
rows.note: This measures a precursor signal, not the formation or removal of a particular circuit. Peak timing is not strongly correlated with eventual grokking epoch (Pearson r = −0.099, p = 0.79; Spearman r = 0.055, p = 0.88).
rows.check: Cv peaks before grokking in 10/10 seeds. However, Cv is a logit-variance signal, not a circuit measure. Peak timing does not correlate with grokking epoch (Pearson r=-0.099).

relationships.condition: Baseline AdamW on (a+b) mod 97, 50/50 split, 10 seeds, 7000 epochs
relationships.reason: Train accuracy saturates within tens of epochs, yet validation crosses 0.95 only at epochs 2962-5301 (r4, r7, r10, r13, r16, r19, r22, r25, r28, r31). Delayed grokking also occurs under the CvAdamW variants.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated within tens of epochs, while validation crossed 95% at epochs 2,962–5,301, with delayed grokking also appearing under CvAdamW variants.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Baseline AdamW on (a+b) mod 97, 50/50 split, 10 seeds, 7000 epochs
source_check.reason: Figure 1 describes early training saturation and delayed validation improvement; Table 1 gives baseline grokking epochs of 2962–5301. Training-set-size dependence remains untested.

relationships.reason: A continuous signal (attention-logit variance) peaks before the jump in 10/10 seeds, with a mean lead of 2400 epochs (r35).
relationships.display_finding: Attention-logit variance peaks before the accuracy jump in 10/10 seeds, with a mean lead of 2,400 epochs.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: r35 supports the continuous-precursor component: the smoothed attention-variance peak precedes grokking in 10/10 seeds. Circuit formation and memorizing-component removal are untested.

relationships.reason: The Cv peak timing is uncorrelated with grokking epoch (Spearman r=0.055), so it anticipates the jump only qualitatively, not when it will happen (r35).
relationships.display_finding: Cv peak timing had Spearman r=0.055 with grokking epoch, providing a qualitative precursor without forecasting when the jump would occur.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The reported Spearman correlation is correct, but V2 requires anticipation of the jump, not prediction of its epoch. Failure to forecast timing does not establish a limitation of V2 as written.

relationships.condition: Single seed, 4000-epoch budget, weight decay raised after memorization
relationships.reason: Raising weight decay (step to 1.0, or proportional up to 1.61) yields grokking within the budget where the baseline does not (r2, r3). This is single-seed and has no weight-decay schedule control.
relationships.display_finding: In a single-seed experiment, stepping weight decay to 1.0 or increasing it proportionally up to 1.61 enabled grokking within 4,000 epochs, whereas the baseline failed.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Single seed, 4000-epoch budget, weight decay raised after memorization
source_check.reason: r2 and r3 support the weight-decay component: increased decay enables generalization within the budget where baseline remains at chance. Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, and ungrokking are untested.

relationships.reason: Extra weight decay gives only a modest, statistically mixed speedup: 6% mean, 8/10 seeds, t-test p=0.060 (r34). The continuous variant shows no mean gain.
relationships.display_finding: Extra decay yielded a 6% mean speedup in 8/10 paired seeds with t-test p=0.060, while the continuous variant showed no mean gain.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r34 shows a small, protocol-dependent latency benefit with mixed statistical evidence; Table 1 gives continuous-sensor mean latency 4333 versus baseline 4313. This qualifies the tested acceleration effect, without testing the circuit-efficiency mechanism.
